content: Vaginal atrophy is a common condition experienced by postmenopausal women, characterized by symptoms such as vaginal dryness, itching, discomfort, and painful intercourse. Systemic treatments, such as oral hormone replacement therapy, are not always necessary for managing these symptoms. An alternative approach involves the use of oestrogenic preparations administered directly into the vagina. These preparations are available in various forms, including creams, pessaries, tablets, and oestradiol-releasing rings. This document is an updated version of a Cochrane systematic review, originally published in October 2006, which evaluates the efficacy and safety of these intravaginal oestrogenic treatments. The primary objective of this review was to assess and compare the effectiveness and safety of different intravaginal oestrogenic preparations in alleviating the symptoms of vaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women. The review included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared these treatments over a minimum duration of 12 weeks. The primary outcomes assessed were participant-reported symptom improvement and changes in endometrial thickness. Secondary outcomes included clinician-assessed symptom improvement, other adverse events (e.g., breast-related issues such as pain or enlargement), and adherence to treatment. The review included 30 RCTs involving 6,235 women. The quality of evidence ranged from low to moderate, primarily due to poor reporting of study methods and imprecision in the results. The findings are summarized as follows: 1. Oestrogen Ring vs. Other Regimens When comparing the oestrogen ring to oestrogen cream, there was no significant difference in participant-reported symptom improvement (odds ratio [OR] 1.33, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.80 to 2.19; low-quality evidence). Similarly, no significant difference was observed between the oestrogen ring and oestrogen tablets (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.15; low-quality evidence). However, a higher proportion of women reported symptom improvement with the oestrogen ring compared to placebo (OR 12.67, 95% CI 3.23 to 49.66). Regarding endometrial thickness, women using oestrogen cream were more likely to show an increase in thickness compared to those using the oestrogen ring (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.94; low-quality evidence). This may be attributed to the higher doses of cream used. 2. Oestrogen Tablets vs. Other Regimens There was no significant difference in symptom improvement between oestrogen tablets and oestrogen cream (OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.55 to 2.01; low-quality evidence). A higher proportion of women reported symptom improvement with oestrogen tablets compared to placebo when using a fixed-effect model (OR 12.47, 95% CI 9.81 to 15.84; low-quality evidence). However, this difference was not observed when using a random-effects model (OR 5.80, 95% CI 0.88 to 38.29). No significant difference was found in the likelihood of increased endometrial thickness between oestrogen tablets and oestrogen cream (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.06 to 1.60; low-quality evidence). 3. Oestrogen Cream vs. Other Regimens When comparing oestrogen cream to isoflavone gel, there was no significant difference in symptom improvement (OR 2.08, 95% CI 0.08 to 53.76; low-quality evidence). However, more women reported symptom improvement with oestrogen cream compared to placebo (OR 4.10, 95% CI 1.88 to 8.93; low-quality evidence). None of the studies in this comparison reported data on endometrial thickness. In conclusion, there was no evidence to suggest a difference in efficacy between the various intravaginal oestrogenic preparations when compared directly with each other. However, low-quality evidence indicates that these treatments are more effective than placebo in improving symptoms of vaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women. There is also low-quality evidence suggesting that oestrogen cream may be associated with an increase in endometrial thickness compared to the oestrogen ring, potentially due to higher doses of the cream. Overall, no significant differences in adverse events were observed between the different oestrogenic preparations or when compared to placebo.
